content: 1. Bishai DM conducted a study in 2007 that evaluated the cost-effectiveness of using misoprostol to manage postpartum hemorrhage in low-resource settings, published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics. 2. Lubinga SJ, Atukunda EC, Wasswa-Ssalongo G, and Babigumira JB explored the potential cost-effectiveness of distributing misoprostol during prenatal care to prevent postpartum hemorrhage in Uganda. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2015, with an erratum issued in 2016. 3. Lang DL, Zhao FL, and Robertson J performed a cost-consequence analysis of misoprostol for preventing postpartum hemorrhage in low-resource settings. Their research was published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2015. 4. Sutherland T, Meyer C, Bishai DM, Geller S, and Miller S analyzed the cost-effectiveness, mortality reduction, and morbidity reduction of community-based distribution of misoprostol for the prevention or treatment of postpartum hemorrhage. This study was published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2010. 5. Sutherland T and Bishai DM examined the cost-effectiveness of misoprostol and prenatal iron supplementation as interventions to reduce maternal mortality during home births in rural India. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2009. 6. Vlassoff M, Diallo A, Philbin J, Kost K, and Bankole A assessed the cost-effectiveness of two interventions aimed at preventing postpartum hemorrhage in Senegal. Their study was published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2016. 7. Diop A, Daff B, Sow M, Blum J, Diagne M, Sloan NL, and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial comparing the use of oxytocin via Uniject (a prefilled single-use injection device) with oral misoprostol for preventing postpartum hemorrhage at the community level. The results were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2016. 8. Gallos ID, Williams H, Price MJ, Pickering K, Merriel A, Tobias A, and colleagues performed a network meta-analysis and cost-effectiveness analysis of uterotonic drugs for preventing postpartum hemorrhage. This research was published by the National Institute for Health Research in London in 2018. 9. Pichon-Riviere A, Glujovsky D, Garay OU, Augustovski F, Ciapponi A, Serpa M, and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of using oxytocin in a Uniject disposable auto-disable injection system compared to standard use for preventing postpartum hemorrhage in Latin America and the Caribbean. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2015, with an erratum issued later that year. 10. The One Health Tool provided draft intervention assumptions in January 2016, which were accessed on November 8, 2018. 11. The State of Inequality report on reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health was accessed on November 5, 2018, via the World Health Organization's online repository. 12. The Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage Initiative (POPPHI) evaluated the safety and feasibility of using oxytocin in a Uniject device for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) in Mali. This pilot study was accessed on November 5, 2018. 13. The World Health Organization's 20th Model List of Essential Medicines, amended in August 2017, was accessed on November 5, 2018.
